subject: Aurelia Health — VPC packaging & transition credit playbook

Subject: Pricing question — VPC packaging and migration credit

Hi Irene,

Quick one as we prep for the procurement review next week. We love the Dedicated sandbox you showed us, but before we move to legal we need clarity on two items for Aurelia's CFO: 1) how the platform fee is treated for on-prem vs VPC (is it per-seat, per-node, or amortized over commit?), and 2) whether Redwood provides an explicit migration/implementation credit for customers moving from an existing stack (we have substantial sunk costs in our current infra).

Lydia and I want to model options for the CFO — can you provide a short practical example (numbers) for a 12‑month pilot vs a 36‑month committed deployment showing: gross list price, a plausible discount/migration credit, and resulting ARR/avg monthly cost? A spreadsheet would be ideal.

Thanks — Samir

--

Irene / all — attaching a compact playbook and a worked example (see attached calc). High level suggestions:

- Platform fee treatment: recommend a split model: 70% amortized against committed monthly throughput (metered) for VPC, 30% allocated as an "ops/oncall retainer" (flat monthly). For on‑prem air‑gapped installs we treat the platform fee as a time‑bound entitlement (annual) with an option to amortize across a 36‑month commit to reduce upfront impact. This keeps pricing comparable but preserves ops retainer for support.

- Migration/implementation credit: offer a credit equal to the first 3 months of committed platform fee (capped) for a 12‑month pilot, and 6 months for a 36‑month commit. For strategic enterprise customers (Aurelia size) we can extend to 9 months if they accept a 48% ARR commit uplift (i.e., larger base commit).

- Discount tiers: baseline = list price; Tier 1 (pilot) = list - 18% (pilot intro discount) + migration credit; Tier 2 (36m commit) = list - 28% + 6‑month migration credit + 1 year of extended log retention (ops add‑on). Addendum: discounts are conditioned on up‑front invoicing for platform fee or a committed monthly ACH cadence.

Worked example (see spreadsheet):
  • 12‑month pilot: list platform fee $120k/yr + license $80k/yr = $200k list. Apply 18% pilot discount => $164k. Apply migration credit (3 months platform fee = $30k) => net first‑year cash $134k; effective ARR for year 1 = $164k; average monthly cash hit = $11.2k.
  • 36‑month commit: list platform fee $120k/yr + license $80k/yr = $200k/yr. Apply 28% commit discount => $144k/yr. Apply migration credit (6 months platform fee = $60k) upfront in year 1; amortize platform fee over 36 months for CPU/node entitlements => effective monthly run rate $12k (post amortization).

Attachments: "Aurelia_Migration-Credit_calc.xlsx" (spreadsheet), short one‑pager "VPC_pricing_playbook.md" in the doc links.

Notes: keep migration credit explicit (dollar value) rather than a percentage to make procurement signoff easier. Also obligate a basic SLA addendum for on‑prem installs to avoid open support exposure.

—Vanessa

Subject: Aurelia pricing proposal & next steps (DEAL-17432)

Hi Samir / Lydia — thanks for the quick conversation this morning. Attached is a short term sheet and the spreadsheet Vanessa prepared summarizing the two options we discussed. Highlights:

1) 12‑month pilot (Pilot-12):
   - List: $200,000 first year (platform fee + license).
   - Intro discount: 18% => $164,000 ARR equivalent.
   - Migration credit: $30,000 applied as credit on first invoice.
   - Deliverables: sandbox VPC + 24/7 critical support during onboarding (30 days), one migration workshop.

2) 36‑month committed (Commit-36):
   - List: $200,000/yr.
   - Commit discount: 28% => $144,000/yr.
   - Migration credit: $60,000 applied to year‑1 invoice.
   - Additional: 12 months extended log retention and a dedicated technical account manager.

Contract mechanics: migration credit is a one‑time invoice credit; platform fee amortization per our proposed split (70% metered/30% retainer) will be explicitly shown on invoices. For on‑prem installs, the platform fee will be invoiced annually but can be amortized over the contract term for accounting purposes — we will issue supporting amortization schedule.

Ask: please confirm which option Aurelia prefers (Pilot-12 vs Commit-36) and whether procurement needs the migration credit shown as a line item or a separate SOW credit. If we get confirmation by EOD Nov 6 we can issue an updated term sheet and DocuSign link for signatures.

Attachments: "Proposed_Term_Sheet_v2.pdf", "Aurelia_Migration-Credit_calc.xlsx"

Best,
Marissa
Director, Commercial
Redwood Inference
